headline: US and Iran deal to end war close, but drones shot down near Hormuz
summary: A tentative agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and lift blockades is imminent, despite new military clashes in the waterway.
details: The United States and Iran have signaled that an agreement to end their conflict is close, with a senior US official stating that both sides have agreed on a text and expect to sign an initial deal in the coming days.
However, hours after Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi claimed Iran emerged stronger from the conflict, US forces shot down multiple Iranian attack drones heading toward the Strait of Hormuz.
The proposed memorandum of understanding focuses on reopening the Strait of Hormuz and lifting the US naval blockade on Iranian ports, with negotiations on Iran's nuclear program to follow.
Under the draft terms, the US would begin releasing billions of dollars in frozen Iranian assets and waive oil export sanctions in exchange for the reopening of the waterway.
The US administration maintains that this is a performance-based deal, insisting that no funds will be released until Iran performs and ceases funding of terrorist groups.
Disagreements remain over the nuclear program; the US seeks the total dismantling of the nuclear program and destruction of enriched uranium, while Iran prefers down-blending the material.
Israel, which has not been part of the negotiations, has stated it will not be party to the agreement and refuses to withdraw from occupied areas in Lebanon.
The deal could be signed as soon as Sunday, potentially in Geneva, by US Vice President JD Vance and Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf.
caption:
A peace deal is looming, but drones are still falling. The US and Iran are on the brink of an agreement to end their war.

The United States and Iran have signaled that an agreement to end their conflict is close, with a senior US official stating that both sides have agreed on a text and expect to sign an initial deal in the coming days.

However, hours after Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi claimed Iran emerged stronger from the conflict, US forces shot down multiple Iranian attack drones heading toward the Strait of Hormuz.

The proposed memorandum of understanding focuses on reopening the Strait of Hormuz and lifting the US naval blockade on Iranian ports, with negotiations on Iran's nuclear program to follow.

Under the draft terms, the US would begin releasing billions of dollars in frozen Iranian assets and waive oil export sanctions in exchange for the reopening of the waterway.

The US administration maintains that this is a performance-based deal, insisting that no funds will be released until Iran performs and ceases funding of terrorist groups.

Disagreements remain over the nuclear program; the US seeks the total dismantling of the nuclear program and destruction of enriched uranium, while Iran prefers down-blending the material.

Israel, which has not been part of the negotiations, has stated it will not be party to the agreement and refuses to withdraw from occupied areas in Lebanon.

The deal could be signed as soon as Sunday, potentially in Geneva, by US Vice President JD Vance and Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf.
